title: Sonarr
descript: Sonarr is a TV series collection manager. It watches for new episodes, searches your indexers, sends releases to a download client and imports and renames the finished files. This package runs the official LinuxServer.io Sonarr image as a non-root container; its settings and database live in the application data folder, with /media for the library and /downloads for completed downloads. Open the app to add indexers, a download client and root folders.
important: Requires DockerEngine. The app contains no indexer and no download client: add them in Settings, and set a root folder to /media and the download folder to /downloads. Data is in DockerAppData/sonarrdocker; media and downloads stay in the same application folder and are not shared with other apps. Back up the folder before uninstalling with data removal. The page is plain HTTP on the LAN.
release_note: 1. First release: Sonarr 4.0.20 from Docker Hub, running as a non-root container; settings and database in the application data folder, with /media and /downloads mounted for the library.

data_notes: `config` holds the database, settings and logs; `media` is the TV library; `downloads` is where completed downloads land. Back up `config`; the media folders are your own files.
design_notes: **Runs as a non-root container.** Verified on real hardware as uid 1000.
**Three volumes.** `/config` keeps the database and settings; `/media` and `/downloads` give the app a library and a download folder inside its own application data directory.
**Health check** probes the web UI on container port 8989.
**Fixed image tag, never `:latest`**, Docker Hub only, no `privileged`, no `network_mode: host`, no Docker socket, no `cap_add`.
limitations: No download client and no indexer are included; add them in Settings.
`/media` and `/downloads` belong to this app only. They are not shared with the Deluge, Radarr or Lidarr packages - each TOS Docker app has its own data folder.
The page is plain HTTP on the LAN; use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing it to the internet.
Docker applications cannot be upgraded in place in the App Center: updating means uninstalling and reinstalling, which keeps the data folder.
